question.text: The solution of the differential equation <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></math> is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>λ</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ln</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></math> (where, <math><mi>C</mi></math> is an arbitrary constant and <math><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math>). Then, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>λ</mi></math> is equal to

solution.text:
The given equation is 1+1ydy=1+1xdx
On integrating, we get,

y+ln⁡y=x+ln⁡x+C or y-x=ln⁡xy+C
∴λ=1.
